newsitem.title: USA: Advanced Environment fire is deemed arson.
newsitem.headline: Advanced Environment fire is deemed arson.

text.p: Advanced Environmental Recycling Technologies Inc said Tuesday that local authorities had decided arson was behind a December 15 fire at the company's Rogers, Ark., facility.
Initial estimates put damages at $400,000 for structural repairs and up to $1.6 million in equipment and wiring damage, the company said.
The fire is the second at the plastic reclamation facility since September, Advanced said.
The company has suffered five major fires since January 1993, it said.
Company executives have voluntarily taken and passed polygraph tests concerning the fire, and the company has been cleared, Advanced said.
The Rogers facility recently resumed operations after rebuilding from a September fire that destroyed a leased adjacent load-out and storage facility, it said.
Although damage from the most recent fire was extensive to a portion of the facility, a significant portion was not damaged, the company said.
Electricity has been restored to a portion of the facility and the company intends to reconfigure its production line while damage repairs are made, it said.
A portion of the facility is expected to resume operations in three to four weeks, it said.

The company and several shareholders are preparing a reward fund of up to $50,000 for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the person or group responsible for the fire, the company said.
